about: S8's remote rows (tools/session-remote.py). The kernel rows: one boot of PAX's console image each, at one processor, frozen at reset; the pinned gdb's transcript under KVM is the golden. The server rows (kind server): sniff-server on loopback in this host with one static fixture, its client the harness or the pinned gdb

rows.name: remote-kernel-write-mem
rows.skip: sniff has no set command (assignment to memory is a later feature with its own contract)

rows.name: remote-kernel-write-reg
rows.skip: sniff has no set command (assignment to registers is a later feature with its own contract)

rows.name: remote-kernel-regs
rows.skip: sniff does not read a target description's flags types, which gdb's info registers prints QEMU's control and flag registers with

rows.name: remote-refuse-hbreak-no-target
rows.why: gdb sets a hardware breakpoint without a target; sniff's hbreak is a remote target's Z1 and refuses by name where there is none (a process, a core, or nothing)
own: sniff's hbreak needs a remote target (`target remote HOST:PORT`).

rows.name: server-refuse-second-client
rows.why: one client at a time: while the first client is attached, a second gets the stub's E.text reply to its first packet and its connection is closed, sniff-server says so by name, and the first client's session goes on

rows.name: server-refuse-non-loopback
rows.why: the protocol has no authentication and gives whoever connects control of the program: a HOST that is not a loopback address is refused by name and binds nothing, unless --non-loopback asks for it by name

rows.name: server-loopback-default
rows.why: `:PORT` listens on 127.0.0.1 alone, as the kernel's socket table shows, and says so

rows.name: server-idle-cost
rows.why: the loop polls only while the program runs: stopped with a silent client sniff-server uses no CPU tick and at most 2 wakeups in 5 s; running it wakes about ten times a second (its 100 ms wait), never past fifteen; the row states each number

rows.name: server-interrupt-latency
rows.why: the interrupt byte stops a running program with SIGINT's T02 within 500 ms, five times the loop's 100 ms wait; the row states the time measured

rows.name: server-z1-hbreak
rows.why: Z1 sets a breakpoint the stub keeps in a debug register (an execute point): accepted, and the program stops with a trap at it, as through the pinned gdbserver

rows.name: server-fp-write
rows.why: an SSE register written with P reads back with p, as through the pinned gdbserver (on Linux; PAX answers PTRACE_SETFPREGS with EIO, which its own row names)

rows.name: server-fp-tag
rows.why: gdb's ftag is the x87 tag word, two bits a register, where the FXSAVE area holds an abridged byte, one bit a register: the stub turns one into the other both ways, held to gdbserver's reads and its write of 0x3fff read back

rows.name: server-threads
rows.why: a program's new threads are traced from their start: a breakpoint a worker hits stops the program with a trap and qfThreadInfo lists more than one thread, as through the pinned gdbserver

rows.name: server-detach
rows.why: D as gdb sends it (each breakpoint and watchpoint removed first): every thread let go, and the program runs to its end on its own, held to gdbserver

rows.name: server-detach-leftover
rows.why: the stub's own row, with no oracle: D with a breakpoint and a watchpoint still set, which the stub takes out itself, so the program runs to its end; the pinned gdbserver leaves them, and its program never ends on its own (measured), so it is no oracle here
